entities.summary: Semi-legendary king of Uruk (c. 2700 BCE) who became the subject of the world's oldest great literary work. Historical evidence (the Tummal Inscription and the Sumerian King List) suggests a real ruler underlies the legendary figure. In the epic, Gilgamesh is described as two-thirds divine, a tyrannical ruler who becomes wise through friendship with Enkidu, grief over Enkidu's death, and the failed quest for immortality. His story encapsulates the Mesopotamian understanding that eternal fame through great deeds, not literal immortality, is humanity's true destiny.
